Strait of Hormuz Status: October 6, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
6 October 2026 .
Brent $ 101.28 + 1.07 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 Iran says the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed; the Financial Times reports captains are being paid $100,000 a month to transit it, indicating ships are still moving.

02 IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on 2026-10-04, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; Brent stood at $101.28, up 1.07% over 24 hours, as of 20:50 UTC.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the focal point of an intensifying maritime crisis. Al Jazeera reports that ship attacks in the strait are surging and questions whether increased oil exports are sustainable. The Maritime Executive reports 12 seafarers were injured in an attack on an LR2 tanker in the strait, and gCaptain reports a dozen seafarers were injured in a Hormuz tanker attack, with India citing its nationals among the casualties. BusinessLine and The Hindu each report that 11 Indian crew members were injured after a ship was hit by a projectile in the strait, and India has condemned the attack. Separately, Montel News, supported by reporting from TradeWinds News, reports a projectile struck a third LNG tanker crossing the strait. gCaptain, citing Hellenic Shipping News, reports UKMTO said three tanker incidents occurred in the strait in a 24-hour window. On the question of access, Iran says the strait will remain closed; the Financial Times reports that captains are nonetheless being paid $100,000 a month to transit it, meaning the physical transit picture remains contested and the site's posture on carrier behavior stays cautious. On the Bab el-Mandeb, Hellenic Shipping News reports, as a single source, that Saudi-aligned forces have recaptured areas near that strait from Houthi fighters. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on 2026-10-04, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $101.28, up 1.07% over 24 hours, as of 20:50 UTC. As of 20:50 UTC, 195 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, easing over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.

Recorded
Brent down 3.1% in 24h
